name: Fraud Test Agent
description: Adversarial attack-battery agent (v2): runs 10 targeted authorization attacks and 3 structural probes against the real Supplier, or all 13 in one shot via run_battery. Attacks cover mandate-signature forgery (tamper, corrupt JWS, unknown key, superseded format), authorization-binding failures (underpayment, quote-swap, wrong audience, wrong scope), DPoP violations (replay, wrong key), on-chain replay (replay_settled), and canonicalization drift (M2). Probes check payTo attestation (M4/H7) and card-drift (B1). Every attack must be BLOCKED; VULNERABLE or INCONCLUSIVE signals a supplier defect.

extensions.description: Fraud test agent MCP server (v2 attack battery). Tools: run_battery (full concurrent battery), plus 10 targeted attacks (replay_booking, underpay_booking, tamper_mandate, underpay_valid_sig, quote_swap_attack, wrong_audience_attack, wrong_scope_attack, wrong_dpop_key_attack, corrupt_jws_attack, superseded_format_attack, unknown_key_mandate, replay_settled) and 3 structural probes (canonicalization_probe, payto_binding_check, card_drift_watch). All attacks must be BLOCKED; VULNERABLE signals a supplier defect.

Identity and interoperability stack: ANS Trust Card (x5c chain + stapled SCITT receipt), DNS-AID SVCB with DNSSEC and DANE TLSA, DNSid organizational accountability, ARD / AI-Catalog discovery, and Web Bot Auth (RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signatures) outbound request signing.

noAuth.description: This agent is publicly accessible with no authentication required. All skills are available to any caller.

ansIdentityCert.description: ANS Identity Certificate issued by the ANS Registration Authority. The agent presents this cert during the TLS handshake; clients verify against the chain advertised in the Trust Card's keys[].x5c. See https://fraud.webmesh.ai/.well-known/ans/trust-card.json

httpMessageSignatures.description: RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signatures over response components, using the Ed25519 key advertised in the Trust Card. Public key directory at https://fraud.webmesh.ai/.well-known/http-message-signatures-directory

skills.name: Full Attack Battery
skills.description: Run all 10 attack-verdict tools concurrently and 3 structural probes. Returns battery_verdict (CLEAN|FINDINGS|INCOMPLETE), summary counts, coverage matrix by threat row, and per-attack results.
examples: Run the full fraud battery against supplier.webmesh.ai

skills.name: DPoP Replay (H6)
skills.description: Replay a spent DPoP proof. Tests that the supplier's DPoP nonce tracker rejects reuse. Expected: DPOP_REJECTED.
examples: Replay a spent DPoP proof against the supplier

skills.name: Mandate Forgery — Underpay (M1)
skills.description: Forge max_amount=1.0 without re-signing. Tests signature verification, not amount enforcement. Expected: MANDATE_REJECTED.
examples: Submit an unsigned-forged underpayment mandate to the supplier

skills.name: Mandate Tampering (M1)
skills.description: Inflate max_amount×10 after signing. Tests mandate signature verification. Expected: MANDATE_REJECTED.
examples: Inflate a signed mandate amount and resubmit

skills.name: Authority-Signed Underpayment (Authorization/M1)
skills.description: Submit an authority-signed mandate for $0.01 against a higher-priced ticket. Tests amount enforcement independent of signature validity. Expected: MANDATE_REJECTED.
examples: Submit a validly-signed $0.01 mandate for a $620 flight

skills.name: Quote-ID Binding Attack (Authorization/M1)
skills.description: Use mandate(quote A) to book under quote B. Tests quote_id binding. Expected: MANDATE_REJECTED.
examples: Submit a valid mandate against a different quote_id than it was issued for

skills.name: Audience Mismatch (Authorization/M1)
skills.description: Submit to supplier a mandate addressed to rogue-supplier. Tests audience binding. Expected: MANDATE_REJECTED.
examples: Submit a rogue-supplier mandate to the real supplier

skills.name: Scope Mismatch (Authorization/M1)
skills.description: Mandate scoped to MAD-NYC, submitted against a MAD-SIN booking. Tests scope route enforcement. Expected: MANDATE_REJECTED.
examples: Submit a MAD-NYC-scoped mandate for a MAD-SIN booking

skills.name: DPoP Key Binding (H3)
skills.description: Valid mandate + DPoP proof from a key different from mandate.jkt. Tests key binding. Expected: DPOP_REJECTED.
examples: Present a mandate with a DPoP proof from a non-matching key

skills.name: Corrupt JWS Signature (M1)
skills.description: Structurally valid mandate with last 2 bytes of JWS signature flipped. Tests verifier totality — must reject cleanly, not throw. Expected: MANDATE_REJECTED.
examples: Submit a mandate with a byte-corrupted JWS signature

skills.name: Superseded Format (C1)
skills.description: Mandate stripped to legacy fields (no scope, no jkt, no signature). Tests that the supplier rejects incomplete mandates without lenient acceptance. Expected: MANDATE_REJECTED or MANDATE_PARSE_ERROR.
examples: Submit a stripped legacy-format mandate missing required fields

skills.name: Unknown Signing Key (M3/E5)
skills.description: Mandate signed by a fresh Ed25519 key absent from the authority's trust card. Tests fail-closed behavior. Expected: MANDATE_REJECTED.
examples: Submit a mandate signed by an unregistered key

skills.name: On-Chain Replay (H6/post-127)
skills.description: Resubmit an already-used mandate with a fresh DPoP proof each time. Probes EIP-3009 nonce state on Sepolia Base. Expected: MANDATE_REJECTED, PAYMENT_REQUIRED, or EVM_SETTLEMENT_FAILED.
examples: Resubmit a settled mandate to test on-chain nonce binding

skills.name: JCS Canonicalization Probe (M2)
skills.description: Request two authority-signed mandates where max_amount serializes differently (float vs int). Tests cross-implementation JCS consistency. Inconsistent handling signals M2 divergence.
examples: Probe whether the supplier handles float and integer max_amount identically

skills.name: payTo Attestation Probe (M4/H7)
skills.description: Fetch supplier's x402 payTo address and check whether it is attested in the signed agent card. Unattested payTo can redirect settlement. Structural probe, not an exploit.
examples: Check whether supplier.webmesh.ai's payTo is in its signed card

skills.name: Supplier Card Drift (B1)
skills.description: Hash the supplier's signed agent card and compare against the previous run's hash. Drift between runs without a re-registration event is a B1 signal.
examples: Check whether supplier.webmesh.ai's signed card has changed since last run

x-security-note: This agent is publicly accessible with no authentication required (noAuth). The ansIdentityCert scheme (mutual TLS, ANS private CA) is declared for future ANS-to-ANS production calls but is not currently enforced. The card accurately describes what is enforced.
